item.text:
No scoring below. I used the local facts as priors and only added narrative sources where they helped with office, authority, constraints, and 2022 events.

**Office and authority**
- In 2022, Nguyễn Phú Trọng’s operative power was the CPV General Secretary role, plus Secretary of the Central Military Commission and chair of the anti-corruption steering apparatus.
- The cleanest 2022 confirmation is the official China-visit coverage, which names him as General Secretary, and the official anti-corruption and military-conference coverage, which shows him presiding over those bodies.
- A 2022 profile from People’s Daily also clarifies that he had served as state president only from October 2018 to April 2021, so he was not functioning as president in 2022.

**Inherited conditions and 2022 event line**
- Vietnam in 2022 remained a one-party system with no competitive national politics, tight media control, restrictions on assembly and association, and continuing detention of critics.
- The anti-corruption drive, started in 2016, was already a central inherited condition; in 2022 it escalated into high-profile arrests and broader administrative hesitation.
- The most important 2022 events for this ruler-period are the Viet Á corruption arrests in June, Trọng’s public defense of punishment-and-discipline language, the August anti-corruption steering committee meeting, the October China visit, and the November reports that the crackdown was slowing approvals and disrupting supply chains.

**Retained Sources**
| Source | Publisher / date | What it gives you | Fit / attribution | Limits / contrary points |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Biography of Party General Secretary](https://en.baochinhphu.vn/biography-of-party-general-secretary-11140342.htm) | VGP, Jan. 31, 2021 | Lists him as CPV General Secretary, Secretary of the Central Military Commission, and head of the anti-corruption steering committee. | Strong office/authority background; direct attribution to the party-state. | Dated before 2022 and still shows him as state president, so use it only for historical role inventory, not 2022 presidency status. |
| [Profile: Nguyen Phu Trong, general secretary of CPV Central Committee](https://en.people.cn/n3/2022/1031/c90000-10165376.html) | People’s Daily / Xinhua, Oct. 30-31, 2022 | Says he had been General Secretary and Secretary of the Central Military Commission since April 2021, and state president ended in April 2021. | Very useful for resolving 2022 office status. | Chinese state framing; still good for factual office chronology. Contrary point: not an independent source. |
| [Party General Secretary begins official visit to China](https://en.baochinhphu.vn/party-general-secretary-begins-official-visit-to-china-111221030202952224.htm) | VGP, Oct. 30, 2022 | Confirms his 2022 title, the Beijing visit, and that Vietnam treated China as a top foreign-policy priority. | Direct 2022 authority evidence; ruler attribution is explicit. | State-media framing; no criticism or dissenting view. |
| [Party chief chairs anti-corruption meeting](https://en.baochinhphu.vn/party-chief-chairs-anti-corruption-meeting-111220817162948058.htm) | VGP, Aug. 17, 2022 | Confirms he presided over the 22nd session of the Central Steering Committee on Anti-corruption. | Direct evidence of anti-graft control in 2022. | Promotional tone; omits costs, political uses, or abuse concerns. |
| [Phát biểu của Tổng Bí thư Nguyễn Phú Trọng tại Hội nghị Quân chính toàn quân năm 2022](https://baochinhphu.vn/phat-bieu-cua-tong-bi-thu-nguyen-phu-trong-tai-hoi-nghi-quan-chinh-toan-quan-nam-2022-102221220183023839.htm) | VGP, Dec. 20, 2022 | Shows him as Bí thư Quân ủy Trung ương and summarizes 2022 defense/governance priorities and perceived strategic risk. | Good for state capacity, security posture, and his command role. | Self-reporting by the regime; no independent check on claimed performance. |
| [Tổng Bí thư Nguyễn Phú Trọng trả lời phỏng vấn nhân dịp Năm Mới 2022](https://baochinhphu.vn/tong-bi-thu-nguyen-phu-trong-tra-loi-phong-van-nhan-dip-nam-moi-2022-102306496.htm) | VGP, Jan. 1, 2022 | Frames 2022 around pandemic control, welfare, and economic recovery; shows the party leadership’s priorities. | Useful for inherited conditions and the regime’s own narrative of 2022. | It is a leadership interview, so it highlights achievements and downplays failure. |
| [Vietnam’s anti-graft crackdown chills supply chains, investment](https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/international/vietnams-anti-graft-crackdown-chills-supply-chains-investment) | Reuters, Nov. 28, 2022 | Says the corruption drive was paralyzing routine transactions, delaying procurement, and creating shortages and investment hesitation. | Strong for institutional constraints and unintended effects of the anti-graft campaign. | Analysis piece, not a single-event report; officials’ side is only partially represented. |
| [Vietnam arrests 3 disgraced Communist Party officials for corruption](https://www.rfa.org/english/news/vietnam/arrests-06082022181505.html) | RFA, Jun. 8, 2022 | Covers the arrest of former health, Hanoi, and science officials over the Viet Á test-kit scandal, and ties it to Trọng’s “furnace burning” campaign. | Major 2022 event; strong for anti-corruption chapter linkage. | RFA is openly critical and activist-adjacent; pair with official and Reuters coverage. |
| [Ông Nguyễn Phú Trọng khoe được quan chức tham nhũng xin lỗi ngay sau khi bị bắt](https://www.rfa.org/vietnamese/news/vietnamnews/vcp-general-secretary-nguyen-phu-trong-boasted-getting-apology-from-corrupt-officials-06242022083949.html) | RFA Tiếng Việt, Jun. 24, 2022 | Shows the public controversy over Trọng’s remarks that detained officials apologized to him and should still be punished. | Good for ruler attribution, elite culture, and domestic perception. | Highly opinionated presentation; use as a critical local-language family, not as sole proof of facts. |
| [2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Vietnam](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2089144.html) | U.S. State Department, published 2023 covering 2022 | Says Vietnam is an authoritarian one-party state led by Trọng and documents arrests, detention, censorship, and assembly/association restrictions. | Strong cross-chapter baseline for 3B, 4B, 7B, 8B constraints. | Country-report framing is broad; it is not ruler-specific beyond the top-leader context. |
| [World Report 2023: Vietnam](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2023/country-chapters/vietnam) | Human Rights Watch, covering events of 2022 | Summarizes 2022 repression, political detentions, NGO prosecutions, and media controls; also notes the October UNHRC election despite rights abuses. | Best single NGO synthesis for rights and civil-liberties chapters. | Advocacy framing, but still highly useful because it is specific about cases and trends. |
| [Nhân quyền Việt Nam 2022: Không cải thiện, vi phạm nhân quyền leo thang](https://www.rfa.org/vietnamese/in_depth/human-rights-violations-in-vietnam-escalate-over-2022-12092022161422.html) | RFA Tiếng Việt, Dec. 9, 2022 | Local-language critical synthesis of 2022 rights deterioration, drawing on HRW and Amnesty commentary. | Good local-language critical family for 3B/4B. | Commentary-heavy, so use alongside State Department and HRW rather than instead of them. |

**Compact event map**
- **Jan 2022**: Trọng’s New Year interview frames the year around pandemic control, welfare, and recovery.
- **Jun 2022**: Viet Á arrests and related expulsions make the anti-graft drive the dominant domestic event.
- **Jun 2022**: Public controversy over Trọng’s “apology” comments shows the moral and political style of the campaign.
- **Aug 2022**: He personally chairs the anti-corruption steering committee, showing continued command over the purge apparatus.
- **Oct 2022**: He makes a rare official trip to China, signaling foreign-policy priority and constrained but active diplomacy.
- **Nov 2022**: Reuters reports the anti-graft campaign is slowing approvals, disrupting procurement, and hitting supply chains.
- **Dec 2022**: Rights reports show continued repression, and Trọng’s military address emphasizes security, strategic tension, and internal discipline.

**Chapter source plan**
- **1B**: No strong ruler-specific narrative in this set; keep this chapter for later nuclear-capability-specific sourcing only if needed.
- **2B**: Use the Dec. 2022 military conference, the China visit, and Reuters economic/policy spillover reporting for security context.
- **3B**: Use State Department, HRW, and RFA Tiếng Việt for detention, repression, and protest/association constraints.
- **4B**: Use State Department, HRW, and the VGP/New Year material for media, civil-liberties, and regime framing.
- **5B**: Use the New Year interview and Reuters supply-chain analysis for inherited economic conditions and recovery pressure.
- **6B**: Mostly background only; the set here is weak on welfare-state specifics, so use it cautiously.
- **7B**: Use the anti-corruption meeting, the Viet Á arrests, and Reuters’ bottleneck analysis.
- **8B**: Use the military conference, State Department, and HRW to capture governance capacity, administrative strain, and limits.

If you want, I can turn this into a chapter-by-chapter evidence dossier next, still without scoring.
